solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Like some music I composed, mostly with style

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word is kept

explanation.surface: A composer boasts of having written in a stylish way.
explanation.walkthrough: The parts are given in reverse order: CLASS comes first, then I and CAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Classical music is a recognised genre, so the adjective describes some music.

clue.text: Plotter caught breaking into Italian's house

indicators.note: breaking into means the letter goes inside the house word

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A conspirator is arrested while burgling an Italian home.
explanation.definitionFit: Casca was one of the conspirators against Julius Caesar, so a plotter.

clue.text: First-rate international body supervises my study

indicators.note: supervises means it is above, coming before in a down entry

parts.note: A, as in A1, means first-rate

explanation.surface: A top international body oversees someone's research.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomy is the study of the structure of the body.

clue.text: Problem about traveller turning up in one high-performance vehicle

indicators.note: about means the problem word goes round the other part

parts.note: a sum is a problem in arithmetic

indicators.note: turning up in a down entry means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: a rep, or travelling salesman, is a commercial traveller
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A problem arises with a travelling salesman in a fast car.
explanation.definitionFit: A supermini is a small car with lively performance, the class above a city car.

clue.text: Sound of alarm near awfully secret Cotswolds location

indicators.note: sound of means the word is said aloud and written differently
awfully means the letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: An alarm sounds near some dreadful secret in the Cotswolds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' turns SECRET into CESTER. The Cotswolds are a hilly rural area of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Cirencester is a market town in Gloucestershire, often called the capital of the Cotswolds.

clue.text: Record — big hit, though not No 1

indicators.note: though not No 1 means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a slog is a big hit in cricket

explanation.surface: A hit record that never reached number one.
explanation.definitionFit: A log is a written record, as in a ship's log.

clue.text: Fellow has work installing air-conditioning

indicators.note: installing means the work word takes something into itself

parts.note: a job is a piece of work

explanation.surface: A man's job is fitting air-conditioning units.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name stands for a fellow, a common crossword convention.

clue.text: Energy drink

definitions.meaning: slang for power or fuel, as in running out of power
liquid squeezed from fruit, a drink

explanation.definitionFit: Juice means both fruit drink and, informally, energy or electric power.

clue.text: Deliver company new logo

explanation.surface: Hand over the firm's new logo.
explanation.definitionFit: To consign goods is to deliver or hand them over to someone.

clue.text: Stay at home entertaining artist and composer

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so the artist goes inside

parts.note: to be in is to stay at home
Max Ernst was a surrealist artist

explanation.surface: Stay at home and host an artist and a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonard Bernstein was an American composer and conductor.

clue.text: Loose woman rejected by theatre cronies

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the letters are read backwards

explanation.surface: A woman of loose morals is shunned by her theatre friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapper is British slang, derogatory, for a promiscuous woman.

clue.text: I'll smile, given Greek meal without starter

indicators.note: without starter means the first letter is dropped, playing on a meal's first course

explanation.surface: Someone promises to smile if given a Greek dinner without the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks as the answer would: one who smiles might say 'I'll smile'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who smiles broadly could describe themself as about to smile, a playful self-description.

clue.text: Who's endlessly keen after start of affair?

definitions.text: Who's endlessly keen after start of affair?

indicators.note: start of means the first letter of the following word
endlessly means the final letter is removed

parts.note: to keen is to mourn or wail

explanation.surface: Asks who is keen once an affair begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the shortened mourning word behind the A; the whole clue also hints at a lover's ardour.
explanation.definitionFit: Amour is a love affair, and one is keen at its start.

clue.text: No drinks served half-heartedly in these?

definitions.text: No drinks served half-heartedly in these?

indicators.note: the heart of the drinks word is a double R; losing half the heart drops one of them

explanation.surface: Wonders whether these places serve drinks only grudgingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' removes one of the two central Rs of SHERRIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosheries are informal eating places, which may well serve no drinks.

clue.text: Strict tutor put out, breathing in a kind of sneezing powder?

indicators.note: breathing in means the rearranged tutor takes the letter in
put out means the letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A stern tutor is annoyed after inhaling sneezing powder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' rearranges TUTOR as UTTOR, which takes in A to give UTATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A sternutator is an agent that causes sneezing, sternutation being the medical word for it.

clue.text: Your daughter's taken round flat

indicators.note: taken round means turned about, so the letters are read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone's daughter has been shown round an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like a home, but it is the definition in its sense of dull or lifeless.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat and dry both describe something dull and lacking interest, as in a dry lecture.

clue.text: Detective is planning to arrest uppity American officials

indicators.note: to arrest means to hold, so the planning word holds the other letters
uppity means upward, so in a down entry the letters read bottom to top

explanation.surface: A detective plans to arrest some arrogant American officials.
explanation.definitionFit: Diplomats are officials representing their country abroad.

clue.text: Iceland free to develop as small part of EU?

indicators.note: to develop means the letters grow into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Iceland is free to grow into a small member of the EU.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ile-de-France region around Paris is a small part of France, hence of the EU.

clue.text: Springing up, American reptile about to kill deer

indicators.note: springing up means rising, so in a down entry the letters read upwards
about means the reptile goes round the killing word

parts.note: gator, short for alligator, is an American reptile

explanation.surface: An alligator leaps up, ready to kill a deer.
explanation.definitionFit: A royal stag is a red deer stag with twelve or more points to its antlers.

clue.text: Tenacity of rebel capturing relative and a few more

indicators.note: capturing means the rebel's name holds the other parts inside

parts.note: Harry Percy, Hotspur, was a famous rebel against Henry IV
sis, short for sister, is a relative
ten is jokingly a few more, as in ten more

explanation.surface: A rebel's doggedness, holding a relative and a few others captive.
explanation.definitionFit: Persistency is a variant of persistence, a synonym for tenacity.

clue.text: Academician put forward, being worthy of respect

parts.note: to table is to put forward a motion

explanation.surface: An academic is nominated, being thought worthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratable means able to be rated, so deserving of esteem or valuation.

clue.text: Speed limit one partly ignored

indicators.note: partly ignored means part of each word is left out, leaving a run of letters inside

explanation.surface: A speed limit that one partly disregards.
explanation.walkthrough: A ton is British slang for 100 mph.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing a ton means travelling at a hundred miles an hour, so the word stands for a speed.

clue.text: Leading team cut

explanation.surface: The leading team is reduced.
explanation.definitionFit: Topside is a cut of beef from the hindquarter.

clue.text: Moving at a fairly fast paceu, or running

definitions.text: Moving at a fairly fast paceu
definitions.meaning: trotting along, faster than a walk; 'paceu' is a typo for pace
running as in consecutively, one after another

explanation.surface: Describes moving briskly, or running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paceu' is a misprint for 'pace' in the source. The second sense is British: three wins on the trot means three in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both trotting along briskly and in succession, as in three wins in a row.

clue.text: Tenant not the first to cross the threshold

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A tenant other than the first moves into a house.
explanation.definitionFit: To go into a room or house is to step over its threshold.

clue.text: Readily believe in return of future monarch?

indicators.note: return means the letters come back in reverse order

parts.note: pupal means of a pupa, which will become a monarch butterfly

explanation.surface: Someone eagerly trusts in the coming back of a future king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'monarch' suggests royalty but is the butterfly; its pupa is the future monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: To lap up a story is to accept it eagerly and uncritically, an idiom.

clue.text: Secretary right, say, to pick up message on this?

parts.note: PA is a personal assistant, a secretary

indicators.note: to pick up means lifted, so in a down entry the letters read upwards

explanation.surface: A secretary checks a device for messages.
explanation.definitionFit: A pager is a bleeper that receives short messages.

clue.text: Umpire given a mouthful between runs?

indicators.note: between means the mouthful sits inside the two letters for runs

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs, here twice

explanation.surface: A cricket umpire snacks between runs being scored.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter is one who judges disputes, as an umpire does in sport.

clue.text: Pole travelled, avoiding east

indicators.note: avoiding means leaving out the given letter

explanation.surface: A Polish person travelled but kept away from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person but is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod is a pole or long thin stick; it is also an old unit of length equal to a pole.

clue.text: Youngster can initially grasp one element of arithmetic?

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: initially means just the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A child can grasp a basic piece of arithmetic.
explanation.walkthrough: To tot up is British for adding up.
explanation.definitionFit: Totting, adding numbers up, is one of the basic operations of sums.

clue.text: Portion of asparagus, singular accompaniment for fruit

indicators.note: accompaniment for means the singular letter goes alongside the fruit, in front

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A serving of asparagus, offered alone alongside fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A single shoot of asparagus is called a spear.

clue.text: New guide about royal city of old required

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the royal letters
new means the letters are made afresh in a different order

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the queen or royal
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A new guidebook to an ancient royal city is essential reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges GUIDE as DIGUE, which goes 'about' ER to make DERIGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means required by etiquette or fashion, obligatory.
